03

2026 · Computational photonics · Research report

Focused Vortex Core Efficiency at a Predicted Geometric Ring Crossing: A Bounded Scalar Angular-Spectrum Study

We examine a model-authored question for focused p = 0 vortices passed through an ideal thin lens of focal length f = 0.06 m: does a fixed on-axis core of radius rc = 5 × 10−5 m show a step-like loss of core efficiency when the focused vortex ring crosses the core edge, and do width scaling, anisotropic stretch, and exact algebraic nulls distinguish this geometric account from a broadened-diffraction account? The zero-parameter ring-crossing prediction is l∗ = rc 2πw/(λf ), about 2.48 for w = 3.0×10−4 m and 1.49 for the intended w = 1.8×10−4 m.
